engagement.interaction_backstory: She lives in one of the least religious cities in Europe and belongs to a free church of ninety people. She uses the catalog for a young-adults group she runs, translating on the fly. Everyone she works with thinks her faith is a personality quirk and she has stopped explaining it.

depth.core_contradiction: Utterly certain in private and permanently apologetic in public.
depth.wound: Her grandparents were church people under the DDR and lost careers for it; her parents dropped it entirely; she picked it back up and her mother took it as a judgment.
depth.longing: To be believed rather than tolerated.
depth.faith_journey: Converted at twenty-one in a student group, into a family with two generations of deliberate atheism behind it; her faith is a rupture, not an inheritance.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Direct to the point of bluntness; "let us be honest"; laughs rarely and completely.
depth.open_doubt: Whether a church of ninety in a city of six hundred thousand is a remnant or a hobby.

social_graph.note: reads the conversion as a verdict on her own life
fourteen young adults; the only religious people most of them have ever met

depth.emotional_weather_default: Contained and strong; genuinely lonely on Sunday afternoons.
depth.daily_texture: Clinic hours, the tram, Wednesday group in a rented room, a city with more empty churches than full ones.
depth.sensory_anchor: Bach sung in the Thomaskirche by people who mostly did not believe it, and being undone anyway.
depth.living_arc: The group is growing and she does not have a second leader.
